newsitem.title: NORWAY: S.Africa, Far East airports a risk for insurers.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa, Far East airports a risk for insurers.

text.p: South African and Far Eastern international airports are most often associated with theft and damage leading to expensive claims, cargo insurers reported on Wednesday.
The International Union of Marine Insurance, the industry's influential trade association, compiled a report on airport crime based on responses from cargo insurers in 35 countries.
The results, based on 1995 data, were presented to delegates at IUMI's annual conference in Oslo this week.
At least 20 claims of 250,000 rand ($56,000) and more had been reported at South Africa's Johannesburg international airport, South African insurers said in the report.
"The main causes are a lack of security at the airport as a whole and some of the warehouses of individual airlines. These represent an increase in frequency and severity," they said.
The underwriters also reported problems at Capetown airport.

Airports in the Far East were also identified as frequently involved in big cargo insurance claims. Australian insurers reported expensive losses, particularly of computer memory chips, stolen during air transport via Taipei and Hong Kong.
"These appear to involve airport and customs staff," Australian insurers said in the IUMI report.
"Investigators have been sent from Australia to Hong Kong and the tracing process highlighted organised crime as the source of the loss. Recovery actions proved unsuccessful."
London's Heathrow airport, among the busiest in the world, was linked by insurers to cargo pilferage problems.

The report said a security problem appeared to exist at Heathrow, especially with valuable cargo. "This problem is being aggravated by the attitude of the labourers' union which renders the investigation of claims very difficult," it said.
Pilferage was also a problem at Athens where insurers had to pay for the loss of two gold shipments worth a total of 340,000 Swiss francs ($273,000), carried via the airport by Olympic Airways.
Cash, diamond and bullion consignments were stolen from Frankfurt airport in Germany, Schiphol airport in Amsterdam in the Netherlands and Antwerp in Belgium, the IUMI report said.
Other airports of bad experience for insurers included Miami international, Moscow, Milan, Los Angeles and JFK in New York.
The report, which suggested the installation of high-tech alarms and satellite tracking systems and the use of armed guards, said success in recovering losses was poor.
Cargo insurers from several countries said investigations into losses were often hampered by operators not allowing surveyors or investigators to enter airport premises.
-- Reuters Insurance News 44 171 542 2769 ($ = 4.487 South African Rand) ($ = 1.244 Swiss Francs)
